newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has agreed to a proposal put forward by election watchdog PollWatch seeking the Bank of Thailand's assistance to stamp out vote-buying. PollWatch chairman Saiyud Kerdpol quoted the PM as saying that he aimed to do his utmost to ensure a fair and clean election and that he was pleased to help the election-monitoring agency in every way. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has said that Laos and Cambodia will become members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations before Burma, which needs more time to sort out its "internal affairs". (THE NATION)

- Frantic efforts are under way to prepare flood-control equipment and defences before the first surge of northern runoff expected today. Bangkok Governor Bhichit Rattakul has ordered every district in Bangkok to be prepared for a surge. (BANGKOK POST)

- Promotional privileges given by the state-run Board of Investment during the first three quarters this year rose nearly four percent from the same period last year. Total investment amounted more than 320 billion baht. (MANAGER)

- A committee on trade and the environment is unlikely to submit a substantial report to the first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation this December in Singapore because it lacks support from developed member countries. (BANGKOK POST)
